Respected Sir/Madam,


I enrolled in the Bachelor of Software Engineering Honours degree programme, and now I am planning to exit from the Higher Diploma level. I have already completed some Level 5 subjects as well. resources.title: Warning on exam offences
resources.description: Please note that any method of copying; writing notes on admission card, record book etc or copying from a nearby person, keeping a mobile device or smart device (even switched off) etc are all considered as exam offences. You must not bring any mobile phones or smart devices to keep with you even switched off, and must be kept inside a bag and in a seperarte space allocated. Please read the instructions sent by the exam division carefully in this regard. During the exam time, supervisor or invigilators may report these malpractices as well as other students. report. After the exam also we receive complaints from students and those are also reported to the exam division. Even at the time of marking, marking examiners may also note and report copied answer scripts. Any exam offence notified will be investigated and if found guilty, you may get suspension from the university upto two years!. That means you cannot do any activity during that period, will lose access to MyOUSL, LMS etc. It is too late to regret your actions after the inquiry and when you receive the punishment. Therefore, please don't get involved in any exam offence. All the best with the upcoming final exams !

resources.title: Information regarding industrial training
resources.description: It is strongly advised not to start training without registering for EEW5611 because those who have started training without pre-requisites have failed to answer questions at viva voce successfully. At recent final evaluation it was noted that a few students who have started training without proper technical knowledge have not been given any proper work by the company and have done only documentation at the work place. T2T programme done without registering for training course will not be accepted in future due to the same reasons mentioned above. If you are already working, or have secured an internship matching the guidelines given for EEW5611, You have to request training exemption. For that you must have worked more than one year in the software industry. How to request exemptions is given in the LMS for the training course. You can request it only after registering for the course. You may work at any capacity, if you get a job/internship in the IT field. Having working experience will increase your chances of securing a proper training place soon. All training places are given by software companies after an interview/ a series of interviews and/or a test. It is very important to pass English courses and Communication skills course (AGM3263) to be in a better position to find a training placement. Just because you have enrolled in BSEHons, you will not get a training place. It will be based on your programming skills, communication skills and attitude towards work.

resources.description: 📑 Milestone 5: Project Progress Report Submission 📅 Submission Deadline: On or Before 10th October 2026 ⚠ Late Submission Policy - 20 marks will be deducted for each day of delay during the first 10 days. - NO marks will be awarded for submissions received after 10 days from the deadline. 📤 Submission Requirements ✅ Upload PDF files only ✅ Supervisor's signature is mandatory ✅ Every group member must upload the report individually ✅ All members may upload the same approved document 📖 Progress Report Structure 📝 Introduction & Background 1 Page 🎯 Problem Statement & Project Objectives 1 Page 🔍 Similar Existing Systems 1 Page 💡 Proposed Solution (Main Use Case Diagram) 1 Page ⚙ Technology Plan (Backend / Frontend / Tools) 1 Page 📈 Project Progress 1 Page 📅 Project Timeline & Conclusion 1 Page 📎 Appendix (Compulsory) Software Requirements Specification (SRS) Monthly Retrospective Reports Evidence of Project Governance Tool Usage (JIRA) Evidence of Git Repository Usage CMMI Meeting Minutes 🤖 AI Usage Declaration If AI tools were used during the project, clearly mention: AI tools used Purpose of use Generated outputs How the outputs were verified and refined by the team Examples: ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, GitHub Copilot, Cursor AI, Figma AI, Lucidchart AI, Visual Paradigm AI. 👨‍🏫 Supervisor Approval Required Before submission: ✔ Meet your supervisor ✔ Obtain feedback on the report ✔ Revise the report accordingly ✔ Obtain supervisor approval and signature ⚠ Reports submitted without the Supervisor's signature will NOT be accepted. 🌟 A well-prepared progress report demonstrates your project's maturity, planning discipline, and development progress. ```

FDE3022/FDE3023– EfIL 2025-2026– Ice Breaker Session

 

Dear Students,

I welcome you to the Faculty of Engineering Technology, the Open University of Sri Lanka.

The EfIL session starts with the Icebreaker (IB) module on 11.03.2026 (Wednesday) at 12.00 PM – 3.00 PM after the Inauguration event. The session on 16th March will be held from 9.00 a.m. to 12.30 p.m. at the Conference Hall, Colombo Regional Centre.
Details of the venues for the other dates will be informed later.

The same session will also be conducted on the same dates at the following Regional Centres. Therefore, students may participate from the centre convenient to them.

Kandy Regional Centre
Matara Regional Centre
Jaffna Regional Centre
Batticaloa Regional Centre
Ratnapura Regional Centre
Kurunegala Regional Centre
Badulla Regional Centre
Anuradhapura Regional Centre

Students enrolled in the following programmes are invited to attend:

• Bachelor of Science Honours  in Textile and Clothing Engineering

• Bachelor of Industrial Studies Honours in Apparel Production and Management Specialization or Textile Manufacture Specialization or Fashion Design and Product Development Specialization

• Advanced Certificate in Apparel Technology

The centre selection details are available in the Faculty Common Course under the Department of Textile and Apparel Technology Section.

We look forward to seeing you on 16th March and the other scheduled dates.

Thank you.

Department of Textile and Apparel Technology

This course is available in the ‘’OULMS’’ online Learning Management System. Please use the following information to log into your online course.

Instructions for logging in:

Web Address:  https://oulms.ou.ac.lk

Type the URL https://oulms.ou.ac.lk/ and go to the LMS.
Click the “Log in” from the top right corner as marked in red colour.
From the landed web page click on “IAM OUSL LMS User” 
Type your credentials on the textfields as given below

Username: ‘s’ number (SID) given in the student’s record book  Password:  Capital U + National Identity card number (U+NIC)

 (For Old NICs use Capital V too)

. E.g:- U899912345V or U198999123456

 

Click on the “Forget password” if password is incorrect

 

From the landing page type the existing email address and click on “Submit button”

A new OUSL email address is assigned to all of you. That is ‘YourSID@ousl.lk’. For all official correspondence, please use this OUSL email. Same login credentials given above are applicable to access your new email (Username: SID, Password: NIC). This email is transferred into your ‘OULMS’ online profile too. If you have problems in logging in and accessing your online course(s) please send an email to ithelpdesk@ou.ac.lk.

Hope you would have a rewarding and meaningful learning experience online!

updates.content:
We warmly welcome you to the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering. As a student of this department, you will explore the principles and technologies that power modern society from electrical energy systems and electronics to computer systems and intelligent technologies.

Our programmes are designed to provide a strong foundation in engineering theory together with practical skills, innovation, and problem-solving abilities.

We encourage you to actively engage in your learning, collaborate with your peers, and make full use of the academic support provided by our staff.

We wish you a rewarding and successful journey in your studies and future engineering career.

Username: ‘s’ number (SID) given in the student’s record book  Password:  Capital U + National Identity card number (U+NIC)  (For Old NICs use Capital V too)

. E.g:- U899912345V or U198999123456

Click on the “Forget password” if password is incorrect
From the landing page type the existing email address and click on “Submit button”
If you are a registered student, you have received the forgot password link in      your OUSL email address.

A new OUSL email address is assigned to all of you. That is ‘YourSID@ousl.lk’. For all official correspondence, please use this OUSL email. Same login credentials given above are applicable to access your new email (Username: SID, Password: NIC). This email is transferred into your ‘OULMS’ online profile too. All ‘OULMS’ notifications will be automatically send to your OUSL email. If you have to clarify anything regarding your OUSL email, please contact: ithelpdesk@ou.ac.lk.

If you have problems in logging in and accessing your online course(s) please send an email to ithelpdesk@ou.ac.lk.

If you have any queries regarding the content of an individual course/ programme please contact the relevant course/programme coordinator.

Hope you would have a rewarding and meaningful learning experience online!

 

Course coordinator

updates.content:
Dear Students 

Build | Solve | Change the World

The IEEE Computer Society 2026 Global Student Challenge (GSC) provides a platform for students from around the globe to create innovative solutions to real-world programming and data analytic problems. For this year’s competition, students in teams of two are required to work on several challenge problems based on real-world use cases and/or real-world data sets provided by various academic and industry teams. This initiative aims to energize students and young professional members of the IEEE Computer Society by involving them in large-scale technical challenges while making a special effort to encourage participation from less-covered regions of the globe.

Link : https://www.computer.org/publications/tech-news/events/global-student-challenge-2026?source=csemail

Head / Mechanical .Eng

The Department Readiness Sessions of the Department of Textile and Apparel Technology will be held on 16th, 23rd, and 30th March and 6th April at the Colombo Regional Centre (CRC).

The session on 16th March will be held from 9.00 a.m. to 12.30 p.m. at the Conference Hall, Colombo Regional Centre.
Details of the venues for the other dates will be informed later.

The same session will also be conducted on the same dates at the following Regional Centres. Therefore, students may participate from the centre convenient to them.

Kandy Regional Centre
Matara Regional Centre
Jaffna Regional Centre
Batticaloa Regional Centre
Ratnapura Regional Centre
Kurunegala Regional Centre
Badulla Regional Centre
Anuradhapura Regional Centre

Students enrolled in the following programmes are invited to attend:

• Bachelor of Science Honours  in Textile and Clothing Engineering

• Bachelor of Industrial Studies Honours in Apparel Production and Management Specialization or Textile Manufacture Specialization or Fashion Design and Product Development Specialization

• Advanced Certificate in Apparel Technology

The centre selection details are available in the Faculty Common Course under the Department of Textile and Apparel Technology Section.

We look forward to seeing you on 16th March and the other scheduled dates.

Thank you.

Department of Textile and Apparel Technology

updates.author: C. H. AMBALANTENNA 21 June 2026
updates.content:
I am writing on behalf of the NDT students to kindly request a reconsideration of the current lab session schedule, exam schedule and CAT exams. As all of us are currently engaged in our internship training, it is unable to obtain leave from our workplaces on multiple weekdays in every week.
 
Therefore, we would be grateful if the lab sessions and exams could be scheduled on weekends. This would help us attend the sessions without affecting our internship commitments.
 
We sincerely request your consideration of this matter and would greatly appreciate the support you can provide.
Please be kind enough to look into this and hope a favorable reply from you.
 
Thank you for your time and understanding.

updates.author: Mr D.S. Wickramasinghe 27 June 2026
updates.content:
📢 Continuous Assessment Test 1 (CAT 1) Timetable

Dear Students,

Please find attached the timetable for Continuous Assessment Test 1 (CAT 1) for the 2025/2026 academic year, applicable to BSc (Eng), BIS, ACAT, and BSE programs within the Faculty of Engineering Technology.

📍 Venue Details

Please note the following venue allocations carefully:

BSE Students: Examinations will be held at all Regional and Study Centres, excluding the Naththandiya Study Centre.
BSc (Eng), BIS, and ACAT Students: Examinations will be held at all Regional Centres, as well as the Gampaha, Kaluthara, Ambalangoda, Monaragala, and Polonnaruwa Study Centres.
⚠️ Colombo Centre Special Notice

For students taking exams at the Colombo Centre, please note that exams scheduled for June 28th and July 4th will be conducted at Mahamaya Balika Vidyalaya, Nugegoda.

📄 Click here to view the Time Table

updates.course_name: FET2025 Common Forum - Faculty of Engineering Technology
updates.author: Miss. R. H. G. Sasikala 9 Mar 2026
updates.content:
FDE3022/FDE3023– EfIL 2025-2026– Ice Breaker Session

 

Dear Students,

I welcome you to the Faculty of Engineering Technology, the Open University of Sri Lanka.

The EfIL session starts with the Icebreaker (IB) module on 11.03.2026 (Wednesday) at 12.00 PM – 3.00 PM after the Inauguration event. The full program schedule is available on the LMS portal under your course. Only the icebreaker , NM and WC will be held as a module with physical presence and all other modules will be conducted online via ZOOM. Zoom links for online sessions will be published in your LMS course.

 

The IB will be conducted in all regional centers and selected study centers listed below. You must present yourself at the nearest or most convenient center, as you prefer according to the following center information.

 

Anuradhapura RC

Rathnapura RC

Matara RC

Badulla RC

Kurunegala RC

Jaffna RC

Batticaloa RC

Kandy RC

Colombo RC

Gampaha SC

 

Should you require further information or clarifications, please post your question in the Student discussion forum in this LMS.

 

 RHG Sasikala – EfIL coordinator for Faculty

Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

	

W.S. Kumari – Member

Dean’s office

Faculty of Engineering Technology




For BSE programme

D.M.P.G.A.S. Dissanayake

Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

updates.course_name: FET2025 Common Forum - Faculty of Engineering Technology
updates.topic: Department Readiness Session – Department of Textile and Apparel Technology
updates.author: Y.S.Y Perera 13 Mar 2026
updates.content:
Dear Students,

 The Department Readiness Sessions of the Department of Textile and Apparel Technology will be held on 16th, 23rd, and 30th March and 6th April at the Colombo Regional Centre (CRC).

The session on 16th March will be held from 9.00 a.m. to 12.30 p.m. at the Conference Hall, Colombo Regional Centre.
Details of the venues for the other dates will be informed later.

The same session will also be conducted on the same dates at the following Regional Centres. Therefore, students may participate from the centre convenient to them.

Kandy Regional Centre
Matara Regional Centre
Jaffna Regional Centre
Batticaloa Regional Centre
Ratnapura Regional Centre
Kurunegala Regional Centre
Badulla Regional Centre
Anuradhapura Regional Centre

Students enrolled in the following programmes are invited to attend:

• Bachelor of Science Honours  in Textile and Clothing Engineering

• Bachelor of Industrial Studies Honours in Apparel Production and Management Specialization or Textile Manufacture Specialization or Fashion Design and Product Development Specialization

• Advanced Certificate in Apparel Technology

The centre selection details are available in the Faculty Common Course under the Department of Textile and Apparel Technology Section.

We look forward to seeing you on 16th March and the other scheduled dates.

Thank you.

Department of Textile and Apparel Technology

updates.course_name: FET2025 Common Forum - Faculty of Engineering Technology
updates.topic: AGI4361 Postharvest Biology and Technology 2025/2026 OULMS course - logging guide
updates.author: Mr. P. K. J. de Mel 17 June 2026
updates.content:
Dear all,

The above course is now available in OULMS.

Logging guide is as follow. 

Regards

P. K. J. de Mel

Dear Students,                                                     

We are pleased to inform that now you can access the following course online.

AGI4361 -  Postharvest Biology and Technology       

This course is available in the ‘’OULMS’’ online Learning Management System. Please use the following information to log into your online course.

Instructions for logging in:

Web Address:  https://oulms.ou.ac.lk

Type the URL https://oulms.ou.ac.lk/ and go to the LMS.
Click the “Log in” from the top right corner as marked in red colour.
From the landed web page click on “IAM OUSL LMS User” 
Type your credentials on the textfields as given below

Username: ‘s’ number (SID) given in the student’s record book  Password:  Capital U + National Identity card number (U+NIC)

 (For Old NICs use Capital V too)

. E.g:- U899912345V or U198999123456

 

Click on the “Forget password” if password is incorrect

 

From the landing page type the existing email address and click on “Submit button”

7. If you are a registered student, you have received the forgot password link in      your OUSL email address.

A new OUSL email address is assigned to all of you. That is ‘YourSID@ousl.lk’. For all official correspondence, please use this OUSL email. Same login credentials given above are applicable to access your new email (Username: SID, Password: NIC). This email is transferred into your ‘OULMS’ online profile too. All ‘OULMS’ notifications will be automatically sent to your OUSL email. If you have to clarify anything regarding your OUSL email, please contact: ithelpdesk@ou.ac.lk.

If you have problems in logging in and accessing your online course(s) please send an email to ithelpdesk@ou.ac.lk.

If you have any queries regarding the content of an individual course/ programme please contact the relevant course/programme coordinator.

Hope you would have a rewarding and meaningful learning experience online!

 

Course coordinator

updates.topic: Welcome to the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
updates.author: Mr.M.S.S. Perera 9 Mar 2026
updates.content:
We warmly welcome you to the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering. As a student of this department, you will explore the principles and technologies that power modern society from electrical energy systems and electronics to computer systems and intelligent technologies.

Our programmes are designed to provide a strong foundation in engineering theory together with practical skills, innovation, and problem-solving abilities.

We encourage you to actively engage in your learning, collaborate with your peers, and make full use of the academic support provided by our staff.

We wish you a rewarding and successful journey in your studies and future engineering career.

Dear Students,                                                     

We are pleased to inform that now you can access the following course online.

EES6214 - Antenna Design (2025/2026)

This course is available in the ‘’OULMS’’ online Learning Management System. Please use the following information to log into your online course.

Instructions for loggin -g in:

Web Address:  https://oulms.ou.ac.lk

Type the URL https://oulms.ou.ac.lk/ and go to the LMS.
Click the “Log in” from the top right corner as marked in red color. 
From the landed web page click on “IAM OUSL LMS User”

       Type your credentials on the textfields as given below

Username: ‘s’ number (SID) given in the student’s record book  Password:  Capital U + National Identity card number (U+NIC)  (For Old NICs use Capital V too)

. E.g:- U899912345V or U198999123456

Click on the “Forget password” if password is incorrect
From the landing page type the existing email address and click on “Submit button”
If you are a registered student, you have received the forgot password link in      your OUSL email address.

A new OUSL email address is assigned to all of you. That is ‘YourSID@ousl.lk’. For all official correspondence, please use this OUSL email. Same login credentials given above are applicable to access your new email (Username: SID, Password: NIC). This email is transferred into your ‘OULMS’ online profile too. All ‘OULMS’ notifications will be automatically send to your OUSL email. If you have to clarify anything regarding your OUSL email, please contact: ithelpdesk@ou.ac.lk.

If you have problems in logging in and accessing your online course(s) please send an email to ithelpdesk@ou.ac.lk.

If you have any queries regarding the content of an individual course/ programme please contact the relevant course/programme coordinator.

Hope you would have a rewarding and meaningful learning experience online!

 

Course coordinator

updates.author: Eng. H.D.N.S. Priyankara 22 June 2026
updates.content:
Dear Students 

Build | Solve | Change the World

The IEEE Computer Society 2026 Global Student Challenge (GSC) provides a platform for students from around the globe to create innovative solutions to real-world programming and data analytic problems. For this year’s competition, students in teams of two are required to work on several challenge problems based on real-world use cases and/or real-world data sets provided by various academic and industry teams. This initiative aims to energize students and young professional members of the IEEE Computer Society by involving them in large-scale technical challenges while making a special effort to encourage participation from less-covered regions of the globe.

Link : https://www.computer.org/publications/tech-news/events/global-student-challenge-2026?source=csemail

Head / Mechanical .Eng

updates.author: Eng. H.D.N.S. Priyankara 24 July 2026
updates.content:
Dear Students,

Applications are now open for the University Student Ambassador National Programme on Child Protection 2026.

As communicated by the University Grants Commission (UGC), applications are invited from 1st, 2nd, and 3rd year undergraduate students who are interested in participating in this national programme.

Eligible students are encouraged to apply on or before 30th August 2026.

Please refer to the attached application form and programme brochures (available in Sinhala, Tamil, and English) for detailed information regarding the programme, eligibility criteria, and application process.

Students who are interested in contributing to child protection initiatives and serving as student ambassadors are encouraged to take advantage of this opportunity.

Application Deadline: 30th August 2026

Registration Link: Call for Applications – University Student Ambassador National Programme on Child Protection 2026

Thank you.

HDNS Priyankara

Head /Department of Mechanical Engineering

updates.topic: Department Readiness Session – Department of Textile and Apparel Technology
updates.author: Y.S.Y Perera 13 Mar 2026
updates.content:
Dear Students,

The Department Readiness Sessions of the Department of Textile and Apparel Technology will be held on 16th, 23rd, and 30th March and 6th April at the Colombo Regional Centre (CRC).

The session on 16th March will be held from 9.00 a.m. to 12.30 p.m. at the Conference Hall, Colombo Regional Centre.
Details of the venues for the other dates will be informed later.

The same session will also be conducted on the same dates at the following Regional Centres. Therefore, students may participate from the centre convenient to them.

Kandy Regional Centre
Matara Regional Centre
Jaffna Regional Centre
Batticaloa Regional Centre
Ratnapura Regional Centre
Kurunegala Regional Centre
Badulla Regional Centre
Anuradhapura Regional Centre

Students enrolled in the following programmes are invited to attend:

• Bachelor of Science Honours  in Textile and Clothing Engineering

• Bachelor of Industrial Studies Honours in Apparel Production and Management Specialization or Textile Manufacture Specialization or Fashion Design and Product Development Specialization

• Advanced Certificate in Apparel Technology

The centre selection details are available in the Faculty Common Course under the Department of Textile and Apparel Technology Section.

We look forward to seeing you on 16th March and the other scheduled dates.

Thank you.

Department of Textile and Apparel Technology

updates.author: C. H. AMBALANTENNA 21 June 2026
updates.content:
I am writing on behalf of the NDT students to kindly request a reconsideration of the current lab session schedule, exam schedule and CAT exams. As all of us are currently engaged in our internship training, it is unable to obtain leave from our workplaces on multiple weekdays in every week.
 
Therefore, we would be grateful if the lab sessions and exams could be scheduled on weekends. This would help us attend the sessions without affecting our internship commitments.
 
We sincerely request your consideration of this matter and would greatly appreciate the support you can provide.
Please be kind enough to look into this and hope a favorable reply from you.
 
Thank you for your time and understanding.

sections.title: Introduction to Common Forum
sections.summary: Welcome to the Common Forum of the Faculty of Engineering Technology. The Common Forum serves as an online platform administered by the Faculty of Engineering Technology, primarily dedicated to facilitating the orientation of newly enrolled students in study programmes offered by the Faculty. Throughout this brief orientation phase, academic activities related to common courses for most specialisations are conducted. These activities aim to acquaint students with the Open Distance Learning mode implemented in OUSL course delivery. Additionally, students engage in the "Student Academic Readiness Training at OUSL" (StART@OUSL) programme during this period, which includes courses "Empowering for Independent Learning (EfIL)" and "English for General Academic Purpose (EGAP)." The Common Forum offers you the opportunity to commence your studies upon enrollment in the courses associated with the following Study Programmes. Additionally, please be aware that access to online courses will be granted separately by April 2026. Until then, use this common forum for all your course-related activities. Bachelor of Science Honours in Engineering (BScHons(Eng)) Bachelor of Industrial Studies Honours (BISHons) Bachelor of Software Engineering Honours (BSEHons) Advanced Certificate in Apparel Technology (ACAT) In this Forum, you can download self-study course material in digital format, alongside various resources and information related to course activities. Since the courses are administered by different Academic Departments, all material and information are systematically categorised based on the respective Departments of Study. Consequently, it is essential to navigate to the designated section corresponding to the Department of Study by which your courses are offered. Select your Department of Study from the navigation menu or move down on the screen. Students can physically meet with academics every Wednesday.

sections.title: Course Section 1
sections.summary: Hello and welcome to the course! You have logged into MHZ3356 - Mathematics for Computing I of the BSE program - This course consists of six units: Logic, Boolean Algebra, Basic concept of Algebra, Sets and Functions, Trigonometry and Introduction to Solid Geometry. Mr G. Nandasena is the main teacher for this course. We are also lucky to have Ms H.P.I. Subasinghe and Ms H.A.M. Hasanthi assisting us with the course. This site will provide you access to the course assignments, marks, notices, sample answers, and many other important details. You are advised to visit this site frequently. We are sure you all will enjoy taking this course and will come up with colors at the end. Good luck, and we're looking forward to our time together! Mr G Nandasena.

resources.title: Start Here
resources.description: Hello Students........👋 You can find course information under different categories in Moodle. Course communication & Course Content & Activities : Under this topic you can find these components Start Here , Announcements , Help Wanted/ Help Given/ Suggestions/ Tips , Course Schedule , Course Outline, Learning Outcomes, Learning Resources, Grades , Past Question Papers. Assignments: In this part you can find all the Assignment in the course. Announcements : You will find posting of current events and up-to-date information about your course. Please check this forum each time you visit the course. Help Wanted/ Help Given/ Suggestions/ Tips : This is where you can post questions or problems regarding technical issues in the use and operation of Moodle. Do spend some time to explore the Moodle environment...you really can't break anything!! If you need some help, choose the "Help wanted" forum. Assignments, Submission Drop boxes and Model Answers : This is where your assignments will be posted. Answers to the assignments need to be submitted before the given deadline as softcopies to the drop-box. You may be asked to post the hardcopy also by the deadline if necessary.

sections.title: Hello and Welcome to the course: MHZ4377 Applied Statistics!
sections.summary: You have logged into MHZ4377 Applied Statistics. This is a 03 credit course offered at level 04 to the Bachelor of Software Engineering degree programme by the Department of Mathematics and Philosophy of Engineering. Under this course we will discuss the basic theories of the statistics and applications of them in real life. We Dr. K. D. N. Kumari and Mrs. B.A.U.Dedunu are the main teachers for this course. We are also lucky to have Ms. E.H.J. Abeyrathna and Ms. C.N.S.Silva assisting us with the course. Begin by clicking the "Start Here" link below - there you will gain insight and information about your online course. At the end of this welcome note, you are highly recommended to log in the OULMS habitually and give your attention to the "Announcements" of this course. I'm looking forward to our time together! Dr. K. D. N. Kumari Mrs. B.A.U.Dedunu

sections.title: EEI4267
sections.summary: Welcome to the course! You’re about to explore how software systems are defined, analyzed, and validated in real-world environments. 🧩 Overview 📘 Course Code: EEI4267 🎓 Level: 4 (Semester 3) ⭐ Credits: 2 📌 Core Course 🗂️ Course Breakdown 🧠 Theory: 10 sessions (20 hrs) 💬 Interactive Learning Sessions (ILS): 3 sessions 🌐 Online Learning Sessions (ONLS): 10 sessions 🧪 Mini Project included 👉 Total: ~95.75 hours 🔹 UNIT 01 Introduction Software Requirements Types of Requirements Functional & Non-Functional 🔹 UNIT 02 Engineering Process RE in Software Process RE Stages Elicitation & Analysis Validation Management 🔹 UNIT 03 Documentation Communication SRS 🧪 Mini Project Analyze system requirements Validate requirements Develop SRS Manage requirement changes 📊 Assessment Structure 🛠 Mini Project (MP) 📝 Continuous Assessment Test (CAT) 🧠 Online Quiz (OQ) 📐 OCAM Formula X = (CAT × 0.4) + (OQ × 0.2) + (MP × 0.4) CAT 40% ➜ OQ 20% ➜ MP 40% ➜ X ⚠ Important Condition ✔ If MP ≥ 40 → Normal calculation ❌ If MP < 40 → X = 0 👨‍🏫 Meet Your Instructor Dr. KVJP Ekanayake |Senior Lecturer ECE Department Academic and Course Coordinator "I will guide you throughout this course to help you gain both theoretical knowledge and practical skills."

resources.title: Contact Information
resources.description: Contact Information Details of the Academic and course Coordinator : Name: Dr. Jeeva Ekanayake Location : Engineering Research Lab, Second Floor -Science and Technology Building, OUSL, Nawala Email: kvpad@ou.ac.lk

resources.title: Start Here
resources.description: 🚀 Getting Started with EEI4267 👋 Introduce Yourself Post in the "Introduce Yourself" forum and update your profile with your own image. 🧭 Explore Moodle Visit the "Help Wanted/Help Given/Suggestions/Tips" section if you need guidance. 📢 Stay Updated Check the "Announcements" forum regularly for updates and notices. 📚 Course Activities & Resources 📌 Study Units Access activities, Mini Project, and submissions. 📌 Glossary Add at least 2 terms under Unit 1. 📌 Online Quiz Check Activity Diary for dates. 📌 Course Outline Review syllabus, eligibility, and assessments. 💬 Need Help? Feel free to reach out anytime. Let’s make this a great learning experience! 🚀

resources.title: Course Outline
resources.description: 📚 Course Structure 🔹 Unit 1 Introduction to Software Requirements Software Requirements Types of Requirements Functional & Non-Functional 🔹 Unit 2 Requirement Engineering RE Process RE Stages Elicitation & Analysis Validation Management 🔹 Unit 3 Requirement Documentation Communication SRS 📌 Course Information Prerequisite: EEX3467 (P) Credits: 2 Total Study Time: ~99.75 hours ⏱ Study Components Studying Sessions: 10 (30 hrs) Mini Project: 35 hrs Interactive Learning Sessions: 6 hrs CAT: 1.25 hrs Online Quiz & Independent Learning 📊 Assessment CAT: 01 | OQ: 01 | MP: 01 Final Examination: 3 hours (Essay) ⚠ Eligibility: (CAT × 0.4) + (OQ × 0.2) + (MP × 0.4) ≥ 40 AND MP ≥ 40

resources.title: Learning Outcomes
resources.description: 🎯 Course Aim & Learning Outcomes Course Aim This course develops students’ understanding of Requirement Engineering by combining theoretical concepts with practical applications in Software Engineering. 🎓 Learning Outcomes Apply requirement engineering theories, tools, and processes Analyze collected requirements effectively Design methods to validate requirements Develop System Requirement Specifications (SRS) Demonstrate knowledge aligned with professional standards 📌 By the end of this course, you will be equipped with both theoretical knowledge and practical skills in Requirement Engineering.

resources.description: 📚 Recommended Reading 📄 Requirements Engineering for Agile Methods 📘 Core Textbook Wiegers, K., & Beatty, J. (2013). (2012) – Software & Systems Requirements Engineering Robertson & Robertson (2014) – Mastering the Requirements Process Cohn (2013) – User Stories Applied Cockburn (2012) – Writing Effective Use Cases What is Agile? | Atlassian Download Center – CPRE 📌 Click on each resource to explore more details or access available content.

sections.title: EEI4360 Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
sections.summary: Hello and welcome to the course! You have logged into the course on introduction to AI Techniques, which is offered to the Bachelor of Software Engineering (BSE) Honours with the course code EEI4360. The aim of this course is to teach students the methods of knowledge representation and Reasoning, classification and clustering and fundamentals of a few artificial intelligence techniques and their applications. This course comprises of 5 main units: Unit 01 Introduction to AI Unit 02 Problem Solving and Search techniques Unit 03 Knowledge Representation and Reasoning Unit 04 machine Learning Fundamentals Unit 05 Ethics and Future of AI I am Prof. Uditha Ratnayake and I am the academic coordinator for this course. If you are here for the first time, begin by clicking the "Start Here" link given under pre-course activities below. There you will gain insight and information about your online course. I'm looking forward to our time together! Uditha Ratnayake (udithaw@ou.ac.lk) Academic Coordinator

resources.title: Introduction to AI
resources.description: Artificial Intelligence is a branch of science concerned with helping machines find solutions to complex problems in a more human-like fashion. This generally involves borrowing characteristics from human intelligence, and applying them as algorithms in a computer friendly way. Computers are fundamentally well suited to performing mechanical computations using fixed programmed rules. Therefore computers perform simple monotonous tasks efficiently and reliably, which humans are ill-suited to. However, for complex problems, computers have trouble understanding specific situations and adapting to new situations unlike humans. Artificial Intelligence aims to improve machine behaviour in tackling such complex tasks. AI is one of the newest disciplines in computing. It was formally initiated in 1956, though work on AI had been under way for about five years. AI currently encompasses a huge variety of subfields, from general-purpose areas such as perception and logical reasoning, to specific tasks such as playing chess, proving mathematical theorems, and diagnosing diseases. Often, scientists in other fields move gradually into artificial intelligence, where they find the tools and vocabulary to systematize and automate the intellectual tasks on which they have been working. Similarly, workers in AI can choose to apply their methods to any area of human intellectual endeavor. Research in AI is aimed at understanding human intelligent behaviour. Humans have an interesting approach to problem-solving, based on abstract thought, high-level deliberative reasoning and pattern recognition. Artificial Intelligence will help people understand this process by recreating it, then potentially enabling them to enhance it beyond their current capabilities. Introduction to Units 1 & 2 Units

resources.title: Introduction to Game Playing
resources.description: GAME PLAYING IN AI Games are well-defined problems that are generally interpreted as requiring intelligence to play well. It introduces uncertainty since opponents' moves cannot be determined in advance. Search spaces for a game can be very large, but human players do quite well without doing much explicit search. They seem to rely on remembering many patterns. Therefore Game playing has emerged as a good test domain for search methods and development of pruning methods that ignore portions of the search tree that do not affect the outcome. The techniques used are typically drawn upon existing methods from the field of artificial intelligence. However, the term game AI is often used to refer to a broad set of algorithms that also include techniques from control theory, robotics, computer graphics and computer science in general. Game playing was an area of research in AI from its inception. In 1951, Christopher Strachey wrote a checkers program and Dietrich Prinz wrote one for chess. These were among the first computer programs ever written. Arthur Samuel's checkers program, developed in the middle 50s and early 60s, eventually achieved sufficient skill to challenge a respectable amateur. Work on checkers and chess were advanced enough to defeat Garry Kasparov by IBM's Deep Blue computer in 1997. The first video games developed in the 1960s and early 1970s, like Spacewar, Pong and Gotcha were games implemented on discrete logic and strictly based on the competition of two players, without AI.

sections.summary: The main goal of Artificial Intelligence is to develop systems that can mimic human intelligence. At the inception of AI it was thought that developing a humanoid robot will be an achievable goal. Even today AI has not been able to capture human intelligence in the full potential, yet many functions of human intelligence have been captured sufficiently. We use Machine Learning techniques that mimic the human intelligence to carry out tasks like classification and clustering. When applying Machine Learning tools, you have to follow a set of steps starting from finding data, cleaning data, separating training and validation data and then applying some model to get an output. Machine Learning fundamentals will be discussed in this week as these are required to carry out the lab 1.

resources.title: Introduction to Expert Systems
resources.description: In artificial intelligence, an expert system is termed as a computer system that emulates the decision-making ability of a human expert. Expert systems are designed to solve complex problems by reasoning about knowledge, like an expert, and not by following the step by step procedures of a developer as is the case in conventional programming. Expert systems are mainly used in two different ways: for decision support and for decision making. ·Decision support: Reminding information or options to an experienced decision maker. Commonly used in medicine. ·Decision making: Allowing an unqualified person to make a decision beyond his or her level or training or expertise. Commonly used in agricultural or industrial systems. Expert systems use symbolic logic, and has an explicit knowledge base understandable to professionals of the field. It has the ability to explain how it arrived at the conclusions in way that is meaningful to its user. Ability to deal with incomplete information is another important feature in expert systems. Development of An Expert System also involves all the steps followed in any computer program. Knowledge Acquisition Knowledge Representation Knowledge Encoding with a specific programming language Expert System Testing and validation Expert System Implementation Basic unit of a knowledge base is a If..Then.. rule. sections.title: EEI4361 - User Experience Engineering
sections.summary: Hello and welcome to the course! You have logged into the course on EEI4361 - User Experience Engineering offered by the BSE programme. This course aims to teach you the concepts of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) with a blend of theory and practice about the study of Software Engineering. This course comprises two main units : Unit 1- Fundamentals of HCI Unit 2- Design and implementation with HCI The first unit presents the basics of Human-Computer Interaction and its main components, namely the Human, Computers, and Interaction. In the HCI Design unit, you will learn about interactive design, user-centred design, usability engineering and evaluation techniques, etc. Begin by clicking the "Start Here" link given under pre-course activities below if you are here for the first time - there, you will gain insight and information about your online course. I'm looking forward to our time together! Mr. Saliya Wickramasinghe Academic/ Course coordinator Contact: bmwic@ou.ac.lk

resources.description: As humans, we can perceive less than a ten-trillionth of all light waves. “Our experience of reality,” says neuroscientist David Eagleman, “is constrained by our biology.” He wants to change that. resources.title: Laws Of UX: Jakob's Law (Law Of Familiarity)
resources.description: Laws of UX is a collection of best practices that designers can consider when building user interfaces. Jakob's law is one of the 20 'Laws of UX' (https://lawsofux.com/). The Laws of UX is a collection of the maxims and principles that designers can consider when building high-quality and engaging user interfaces. Jakob's law states that users spend most of their time on other sites. This means that users prefer your site to 'work' the same way as all the other sites they already know. (Don't make me think.) - Users will transfer expectations they have built around one familiar product to another that appears similar - By leveraging existing mental models, we can create superior user experiences in which the user can focus on their task rather than having to 'learn your version' of things. This concept is also referred to as The Law Of Familiarity. https://www.youtube.com/embed/6RHk9A43dn4

Task Analysis (~5): Logical breakdown of user tasks and workflows. Prototype Design (~5): Usability, structure, and design quality. Evaluation & Results (~5): Testing approach and meaningful findings. Group Work (~10): Collaboration, equal contribution, teamwork, and coordination. Q & A (individual mark) (~30): Clarity, confidence, correctness, and understanding. Report (30): Structure, clarity, technical content, and quality.

resources.description: Read the following instructions before selecting the slot. Please carefully select the date and time for your team's presentation. Note that this choice is final, and no changes can be made once selected. Instructions for Selecting the Presentation Slot: Only the convener (designated team leader) should choose the date and time on behalf of the team(Only one choice from a team); all team members are expected to attend at the selected slot. Each team is permitted only one slot selection, and all team members must be present. Important Notices: If you are unable to attend the viva, you will receive a score of zero (0) for the Mini Project. A score below 40% (<40) on the Mini Project will disqualify you from sitting for the final exams, as it is a mandatory course component. The viva must be attended with your entire team. Presentation Guidelines: You will have 10 minutes to present your work, followed by 5 minutes for a Q&A session. Each team member is required to participate in the presentation. Presentation Content Requirements: Please ensure your presentation includes the following sections: Identified Problem Proposed Solution User Personas (User Analysis) Task Analysis Prototype Design Evaluation of the Prototype Results of the Prototype Evaluation

This is the Object Oriented Design BSE Programme  course from the Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering.

This is a 3 credit core course offered in Level 4.

sections.title: Course Section 1
sections.summary: Hello and welcome to the course! You have logged into the course on EEI4362- Object Oriented Design. This is a level 4, three-credit course offered by the Electrical and Computer Engineering of the Faculty of Engineering Technology, OUSL, for Bachelor of Software Engineering programme. The aims of this course are to give students a good understanding of basic concepts of object oriented design; introduce them to the fundamental concepts of programming and principals of abstraction, modularity and reusability; and to illustrate the object orientation as the basis for designing software systems and applications. This course comprises of Introduction to Overview of programming languages, Programming Concepts, Abstraction and reusability mechanisms, Object Oriented Concepts, Application of Oriented Concepts in programming, Object-oriented Analysis and Design, Design patterns and Frameworks. My name is A.W.M.W.I.B.Atthanayake and I am the academic coordinator for this course. I will be interacting with you in Moodle. You can begin your tour by clicking the "Start Here" link below if you are here for the first time - there you will gain insight and information about your online course. I'm looking forward to our time together, best of luck and happy learning! Academic & Course Coordinators: Mr. A.W.M.W.I.B.Atthanayake Mr. N.M. Siyad

resources.title: Start Here
resources.description: We welcome you to the Virtual Classroom of the Course EEI4362 - Object Oriented Design, and hope you will become a frequent visitor and an active member of the community. As this is your first visit, here are some interesting places you should visit within our page during this and subsequent visits. Course Communication: Under this topic you can find the components Start Here, Announcements, Help Wanted/Help Given/Suggestions/Tips Forum, and Let us Introduce Ourselves. Announcement : You will find posting of current events and up-to-date information about your course. Please check this forum each time you visit the course. Help wanted/Help given : This is where you can post questions or problems regarding technical issues in the use and operation of Moodle. Let us introduce ourselves : This is will be a group wise introduction to each of the group members (students / tutors) Course Information : Under this topic you can find the components Course synopsis, Activity Diary, Course Outline, Course Information and Learning Resources Course Activities : In this part you can find all the materials with respect to each unit, the activities/assignments pertaining to each unit, the Day School materials, lab sheets for the course, and recordings.

resources.title: Learning Outcomes
resources.description: This course will help you to recall the basic concepts of Object Oriented Programming (OOP) you studied in level 3 course. Furthermore, this course teaches you to design software solutions using Unified Modelling Language(UML) and to write programs applying multithreading, design patterns, architectural patterns using industrial frameworks with commonly uses programming languages in the industry. Finally this course will help you to perform as a professional, by applying OOP design concepts using industrially used frameworks and programming practices in industrial projects in the software industry. On the completion of this course student will be able to; CLO1: Apply the basic concepts of object oriented design and programming for a given scenario CLO2: Explain how abstraction mechanisms support the creation of reusable software components CLO3: Perform object oriented design and analysis on real world problems CLO4: Document the design solutions with UML notations and diagrams CLO5: Select appropriate software design patterns and frameworks for different problems

updates.author: Prof.(Ms) U.W. Ratnayake 7 Feb 2026
updates.content:
Dear students,

Please note that any method of copying; writing notes on admission card, record book etc or copying from a nearby person, keeping a mobile device or smart device (even switched off) etc are all considered as exam offences.  You must not bring any mobile phones or smart devices to keep with you even switched off, and must be kept inside a bag and in a seperarte space allocated. Please read the instructions sent by the exam division carefully in this regard.

During the exam time, supervisor or invigilators may report these malpractices as well as other students. report. After the exam also we receive complaints from students and those are also reported to the exam division.  Even at the time of marking, marking examiners may also note and report copied answer scripts.

Any exam offence notified will be investigated and if found guilty, you may get suspension from the university upto two years!. That means you cannot do any activity during that period, will lose access to MyOUSL, LMS etc. It is too late to regret your actions after the inquiry and when you receive the punishment. 

Therefore, please don't get involved in any exam offence. All the best with the upcoming final exams !

updates.topic: Clarification Regarding CAT Exam Center – Ambalantota Not Listed
updates.author: A.H.C. HASANGA 26 June 2025
updates.content:
Dear Sir,


I am writing to kindly seek your guidance regarding my CAT exam center. My originally registered center is Ambalantota, and since I had no intention of changing it, I did not fill out the Google Form intended for students requesting a center change.


However, I recently noticed that Ambalantota is not included in the list of exam centers for the CAT exam , and unfortunately, the Google Form is now closed. As a result, I was unable to submit any request regarding a new center.


Given this situation, I would appreciate your advice on how I can proceed. The nearest available center to me is Matara, and I am fully willing to sit for the exam there if it is possible.


Could you please let me know whether I am eligible to sit for the CAT exam, and if so, where my exam center would be?


Thank you very much for your time and support.


Best regards,
A.H.C. Hasanga

updates.topic: Important infor about new courses in RC '25
updates.author: Prof.(Ms) U.W. Ratnayake 29 Apr 2026
updates.content:
With concurrent registration for EEI4360, re-registering students can get Level 6 courses if you have fulfilled all other pre-requisites.   example - EEI6171, EEI6278, EEI6320 etc
You can register for EEI4360 if you have got CA for MHZ3459 or MHZ4256
MHZ2250 will be exempted if you have passed MHZ3459 or MHZ4256

updates.topic: Google form requesting courses without due pre-requisites
updates.author: Prof.(Ms) U.W. Ratnayake 2 May 2026
updates.content:
Link for accessing the Google form requesting courses without due pre-requisites;

https://oulms.ou.ac.lk/mod/url/view.php?id=163258

Please note that all requests will be considered by a panel of lecturers including the Director and the HoD, and a decision will be given. This facilitation is mainly for those students who have registered or completed the Final Project and/or have come to the last year of study and have some effect due to curriculum change.

Just because you have been registered for 4-5 years, and not being able to pass a Level 3 or Level 4 course, do not request higher level courses. 

Everybody does not have to move to RC'25 either. There are 2 more years - 2025/2026 and 2026/2027 that you can try to graduate by RC (current) curriculum. You have to register for new courses and those will be back converted to mapping RC courses.

[Linked Section Details]:
Course requests without meeting pre-requisites
Completion requirements

Please read the guidelines carefully, and do not request unnecessary override requests.

Please note following and do not make requests related to following;

1.  MHZ2250 will be exempted if you have passed MHZ3459 or MHZ4256 for those transfering to RC'25
2. With EEI4360 Con-current registration (no need for a pass or EL), Level 6 courses like EEI5280, EEI6278, EEI6171,  EEI6320 can be offered only for the year 2025/2026 as this is the first year this course is introduced.

3. If you hope to graduate with RC and need to register for DMM6301 and DMM6302 (equivalent for DMM6602), then you must request

updates.topic: Request to Schedule Future CAT Exams on Weekends
updates.author: S.V.A.U. Piyumali 15 Oct 2025
updates.content:
Dear Sir,

I hope you are well. I wanted to kindly bring up a concern regarding the scheduling of CAT exams on weekdays. 

As there are significant amount of working students, for us it is often quite difficult to obtain leave from work on multiple weekdays to attend the exams.

For example, this week

The four CAT 1 exams are held across three different days - 2 exams on one day (today) and the remaining 2 on next consecutive weekdays. As working professionals it’s not easy to request this many days off within one week and in many cases, these leave requests are not approved. Some of us also manage teams or handle key responsibilities at work, which makes it even more challenging.


While we fully understand that planning the schedule involves many logistical factors, spreading exams across several weekdays makes it challenging for working students to participate without affecting their work commitments.

If possible, wlle would be sincerely grateful if future CAT exams could be arranged on weekends or at least grouped into a single day. This would make it much easier for those balancing both full-time work and studies to attend without difficulty.

We deeply appreciate the efforts of the academic team in supporting us and organizing these exams and we share this feedback only with the hope of making the program more manageable for all working students.

Thank you very much for your understanding and consideration.

Warm regards,
Your students,
BSE 24/25

updates.author: I H D Prasad Madhusanka Iddagoda 16 Oct 2025
updates.content:
​Dear Sir,

​I am writing to bring to your attention a significant scheduling conflict in the official timetable for the CAT 02 examinations for the BSE 2024/2025 Semester 02.

​On Thursday, 14 November 2025, three (3) examinations are scheduled for the same day:

​AGM3263 – Communication Skills (9am – 10.15am)
​EEI4346 – Web Technology (10.45am – 12pm)
​EEX3373 – Computer and Communication Technology (1pm – 2.15pm)

​Having three continuous assessment tests scheduled sequentially on the same day poses a considerable challenge for students in terms of preparation and performance, especially the rapid turnaround between the first two subjects.

​To ease this burden and ensure students can perform optimally, I would like to respectfully request a review of the schedule. It would be greatly appreciated if one of the three aforementioned examinations could be rescheduled to the morning slot on either Friday, 15 November 2025, or Saturday, 16 November 2025, to allow for better spacing.

​Thank you for your time and consideration of this matter.

resources.title: To access the re-sit courses
resources.description: Please follow these steps to access the re-sit courses: Visit the site's homepage. OULMS: All courses Utilize the search function to locate the course using its course code. Once you have found the desired course, click on it. To gain access, enter the guest access password, which is derived from the course code and the format "course code_2024." resources.title: Warning on exam offences
resources.description: Please note that any method of copying; writing notes on admission card, record book etc or copying from a nearby person, keeping a mobile device or smart device (even switched off) etc are all considered as exam offences. You must not bring any mobile phones or smart devices to keep with you even switched off, and must be kept inside a bag and in a seperarte space allocated. Please read the instructions sent by the exam division carefully in this regard. During the exam time, supervisor or invigilators may report these malpractices as well as other students. report. After the exam also we receive complaints from students and those are also reported to the exam division. Even at the time of marking, marking examiners may also note and report copied answer scripts. Any exam offence notified will be investigated and if found guilty, you may get suspension from the university upto two years!. That means you cannot do any activity during that period, will lose access to MyOUSL, LMS etc. It is too late to regret your actions after the inquiry and when you receive the punishment. Therefore, please don't get involved in any exam offence. All the best with the upcoming final exams !

resources.description: Important information about project courses in BSEHons degree programme There are 3 Project courses in the BSEHons degree programme (in old curriculum as well as new curriculum) A project is to be carried out under the guidance of a supervisor. Students must meet the supervisor in-person and must not wait for on-line meetings. For all projects a log book has to be maintained by each student, and it has to be signed by the supervisor at least 3 times before final presentation. Therefore, when you register for a project course, be prepared to travel and meet the supervisor. Every project is about solving a problem. Therefore, before registering you must have an idea what you are going to do. If you do not have an acceptable project proposal/project idea before add/drop, it is advisable that you drop the project course. Unlike the current year, in 2025/2026 all project progress presentations as well as EEY6289 final presentations will be completed before second semester eligibility due date. EEY4189 Group project If you are going to register for EEY4189, first you have to form a group of 4-5 members. All members must be able to meet physically at one center - at least a few times throughout the year. This project could be a simple digitization/automation project but it requires you to provide a solution for an existing (simple) problem with a real client. If you are going to register for EEY4189 in 2025/2026, please form a group and find a client now ! EEY6289 Research Methodology & Project identification If you are going to register for this course, think about an interesting area that you would like to research on. resources.title: Information regarding industrial training
resources.description: You can carry out an internship without registering for EEW5811. However, to come for the assessment you have to register for EEW5811. When the Department send CVs to companies for training, priority will be given for those who register to EEW5811. If you are already working, or have secured an internship matching the guidelines given for EEW5811, You have to request training exemption. For that you must have worked more than one year in the software industry. How to request exemptions is given here. https://ou.ac.lk/industraltd/ You have to download the relevant form and get it filled according to given instructions and submit to the Training Coordinator, who will be appointed by 1st of January 2024. You may work at any capacity, if you get a job/internship in the IT field. Having working experience will increase your chances of securing a training place soon. All training places are given by software companies after an interview/ a series of interviews and/or a test. From the day you joined the BSEHons programme, you were requested to complete Future Career Bridge Challenges and the Communication skills course (AGM3263) to be in a better position to find a training placement. Just because you have enrolled in BSEHons, you will not get a training place. It will be based on your programming skills, communication skills and attitude towards work.

resources.title: Exit (Leaving the degree) with Diploma certificate 2022/2023
resources.description: Dear students, If you wish to leave the degree of Bachelor of Software Engineering, you may do so with the Award Diploma in Software Development. Following are the compulsory courses that you must have completed in order to get the Diploma. In addition to compulsory courses, you must have completed 30 credits. AGM3263 Communication Skills EEI3346 Web Application Development EEI3262 Introduction to Object Oriented Programming EEI3266 Information Systems and Data Management EEX3373 Communication and Computer Technology EEX3467 Software Engineering Concepts and Programming EEM3366 Introduction to Business Studies FDE 3023 Empowering for Independent Learning This is the first time this exit point is offered. From 2022/2023 onwards this exit point is availabe for those who register to Bachelor of Software Engineering degree programme. Please fill this journal form with your registration number and the reason for leaving the degree and apply for the same in the Google form that will be floated by the Exam divison. Please note that filling this journal entry is not enough and you must submit the Google form floated by the exam divison. Higher Diploma in Software Engineering is an internediate qualifictaion that you can obtain after completeing 2 years of academic work and 6 months of training. Even if you request for the Higher Diploma, you can continue with the degree. Therefore it is adviced to obtain the Higher Diploma and continue unless you have a compelling reason to leave the degree programme. To get the HD certificate also you have to apply through the Google form shared by the Exam divison.

sections.title: Economics and Marketing for Engineers
sections.summary: Hello and welcome to the course! Hello and Welcome to the online delivery of AGM4367-Economics and Marketing for Engineers. This is a level 4 course in the management course category in the Bachelors of Software Engineering Honors Programme. This course has been designed to provide the students with a wide and useful knowledge and experience on the basic economic principles and marketing in the decision making process of the engineers. The course materials consist of 20 sessions arranged in three units. We are looking forward to our time together! Ms. Kavini Nanayakkara (Course Coordinator)
